title: Is war between China and the US inevitable? | Graham Allison
summary: A Harvard scholar presents Thucydides's Trap: most past cases of a rising power challenging a ruling power ended in war, and the US and China are on that path unless they find a new way.

assertions.quote: found 16 cases in which a rising power threatened to displace a ruling power. Twelve of these ended in war.

verdicts.note: Allison's Thucydides Trap study counted war in 12 of 16 cases, but critics dispute the case selection and several transitions, such as Britain to the US, were peaceful.

The Belfer case file counts sixteen cases over 500 years in which a rising power threatened a ruling power, and twelve ended in war. That supports 'usual outcome', but the cases were curated by the project with no statistical test.

Hanania notes that adding Belfer's 14 candidate cases gives 19 wars in 30 transitions, and that since the mid-20th century only 1 of 7 (1 of 8 with US-China) ended in war. He argues the case selection is undefined, so war was common in older transitions but is not the usual outcome today.

verdicts.note: 1914 fits, but many power-transition wars were started directly by one of the rivals.

assertions.quote: by 2024, it will be half again larger.

verdicts.note: At purchasing-power parity China was about a quarter larger than the US in 2024; at market exchange rates it was about two-thirds the US size.
US nominal GDP was $10 trillion larger than China's in 2024, and at 2025 growth rates China would not pass the US in nominal GDP until 2041.

assertions.quote: the 100th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic, China means to be

verdicts.note: Xi's stated goals include a world-class military and a great modern socialist country by 2049, which most analysts read as seeking pre-eminence.
DoD 2025: China's national strategy is 'great rejuvenation' by 2049 with a 'world-class' military, and the report reads this as an ambition to displace the US as the most powerful nation.
Davidson: China has long said it wants to supplant the US and its leadership of the rules-based order by 2050, and he worries it is moving that target closer.
US intelligence cites China's goal of 'national rejuvenation' by 2049, which requires unification with Taiwan; being the world's leading power is not stated in those terms.

assertions.quote: without great power war and with more prosperity

verdicts.note: There has been no direct great-power war since 1945, but nuclear deterrence and bipolarity are also credited and the order's role is debated.
Kroenig credits the US-led liberal international system with zero great-power wars over eighty years; an expert's attribution, not a test of the cause.
Clauset: the long peace is statistically indistinguishable from a fluctuation, so the data cannot yet show whether post-war institutions reduced the risk of war.

Braumoeller finds international orders such as the Western liberal order keep the peace mainly among their own members, while raising the chance of war between orders, as in the Cold War; he says the order is now fraying.
